title: Cost before the bill: Infracost, and the resource nobody owns

videos.script: Ana's plan for the shop said eight to add. It did not say what those eight would cost. {{plan}} The answer was already in it. Every machine names its type, and every type has a price per hour. Multiply by the hours in a month, and the bill is known before anything exists. {{price}} A tool called Infracost does that sum on every pull request. A reviewer sees the dollars beside the diff, and a one-word change stops looking small. {{diff}} Then there is the money nobody plans. A disk somebody made by hand. A preview environment nobody destroyed. They cost the same as everything else, and no review will ever show them. {{orphans}} So this lesson does four things. It prices a plan. It tags everything, so the bill can name an owner. It hunts for what has no owner. And it gives temporary environments a date to die. {{tags}} It ends with a budget, written as code, that warns before the month is over. {{budget}}
